name: Impersonation of an authority or bank officer
description: Someone claims to be from the police, a tax office, a regulator or the bank's fraud team and says the customer must pay or move money to stay out of trouble.
signals: Claims to be police, customs, tax, a regulator or a bank officer
Threat of arrest, a frozen account or legal action
Asks to move money to a 'safe' or 'verification' account
Tells the customer to keep the call secret or stay on the line
Asks for an OTP, PIN or card details
customer_question: Would a real officer ask me to send money to a personal account, or could I call the official number myself and check?

name: Fake investment group
description: A chat group or 'mentor' promises high, fast, guaranteed returns from trading, crypto or IPO allotments, often showing screenshots of other members' profits.
signals: Guaranteed or very high returns in days or weeks
Group chat full of members posting profit screenshots
A mentor, professor or 'VIP analyst' giving tips
Pressure to deposit more to unlock withdrawals
Payment to an individual's account instead of a regulated broker
customer_question: Is this platform registered with the market regulator, and can I withdraw a small amount before I put in more?

name: Romance or friendship scam
description: Someone met online builds a close relationship over weeks, never meets in person, then asks for money for an emergency, travel, customs or an investment.
signals: Relationship formed online and moved quickly to private chat
Always has a reason not to video call or meet
Sudden emergency, medical bill, visa or customs fee
Asks for secrecy from family and friends
Promises to repay once a parcel or inheritance arrives
customer_question: Have I ever seen this person on a live video call, and would I still send this if a friend asked me to check first?

name: Task-for-pay job offer
description: A part-time job pays small amounts for simple tasks like liking videos or rating hotels, then asks the worker to pre-pay for 'premium tasks' to earn more.
signals: Unsolicited job offer on a messaging app
Easy online tasks like likes, reviews or ratings
Small early payouts to build trust
Asks the worker to deposit money to unlock higher-paying tasks
Says earnings are frozen until another payment is made
customer_question: Why would a real employer ask me to pay them before I can get paid?

name: Fake invoice or changed bank details
description: A message that looks like it is from a known supplier, landlord or contractor says their bank account has changed and asks for payment to the new account.
signals: Notice that bank details have 'recently changed'
Email or chat from a slightly different address or number
Urgency about an overdue invoice
New payee name does not match the business name
Asks not to call because they are 'in a meeting' or 'travelling'
customer_question: Have I confirmed the new account by calling the supplier on a number I already had?

name: Lottery or prize fee
description: The customer is told they won a prize, lucky draw or lottery they never entered and must pay a tax, processing or delivery fee to claim it.
signals: Prize or lottery the customer never entered
Fee, tax or GST must be paid before release
Official-looking certificate or logo
Deadline to claim
Payment to a personal account or e-wallet
customer_question: Did I actually enter this draw, and why would a real prize need me to pay first?

name: Relative or friend in distress
description: A message from a new number claims to be a child, relative or friend who lost their phone or is in trouble and urgently needs money.
signals: Message from a new or unknown number claiming to be family
'Lost my phone' or 'this is my new number'
Urgent need: hospital, accident, police, rent
Asks not to call because they cannot talk right now
Payment to someone else's account
customer_question: Have I called this person on their old number or spoken to them by voice to confirm it is really them?

name: Parcel or customs fee
description: A courier or customs message says a parcel is held and a small fee, duty or address update payment is needed, or that a parcel in the customer's name contains illegal items.
signals: Held parcel the customer was not expecting
Small redelivery, duty or address fee
Link to a payment page that is not the courier's site
Claim that a parcel in their name contains illegal goods
Transfer to 'clear' the case or customs
customer_question: Was I expecting this parcel, and does the tracking number work on the courier's official website?

name: Loan processing fee
description: An easy loan is approved with no checks, but the borrower must pay a processing, insurance or GST fee before the money is released.
signals: Instant approval without credit checks
Upfront processing, insurance or file fee
Lender not a known bank or registered lender
Fee paid to an individual's account
More fees requested after the first one
customer_question: Is this lender registered, and why is the fee not simply deducted from the loan amount?

name: Remote access support
description: A fake support agent for a bank, telecom or tech company asks the customer to install a screen-sharing app to 'fix' a problem or process a refund.
signals: Asks to install a screen-sharing or remote control app
Refund, KYC update or account problem as the reason
Asks the customer to log in to banking while sharing the screen
'Accidental' over-refund that must be sent back
Asks for OTPs read out loud
customer_question: Did I contact this support team myself, and why would they need control of my phone to help me?

name: Marketplace advance payment
description: A seller or buyer on an online marketplace asks for an advance, token amount or 'delivery charge' before the item is seen, often posing as army or transfer staff.
signals: Price well below market value
Seller cannot meet in person; says they are posted elsewhere
Advance, token or courier charge before delivery
Buyer sends a QR code to 'receive' money
Pressure because 'many others are interested'
customer_question: Can I see the item or pay on delivery instead of paying in advance to a stranger?

name: Utility disconnection threat
description: A message says electricity, gas, water or mobile service will be cut tonight unless an overdue bill is paid immediately to a given number or account.
signals: Disconnection 'tonight' or within hours
Bill not updated or overdue, with no bill reference the customer recognises
Message from a personal mobile number
Asks to call an 'officer' or pay to a personal account
Asks to install an app to pay
customer_question: Does my bill on the utility's official app or website actually show an overdue amount?
